newsitem.title: CANADA: Abacan falls after cash flow warning.
newsitem.headline: Abacan falls after cash flow warning.

text.p: Investors lopped more than 40 percent of the value off Abacan Resource Corp stock on Monday after the Calgary-based oil company said its 1997 cash flow would be much lower than analysts' expectations.

Abacan, which is developing oil prospects on the west African coast, said it would pump out lower than projected cash flow because of reduced average production, lower world oil prices and higher than expected project startup costs.
Abacan shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange fell 3.44 to 4.66 on volume of more than one million shares in early trade.
The company's Nasdaq-listed shares were down 2-7/16 to 3-3/8 on 2.3 million shares.

Abacan said average production would be lower in June than in May due to "natural declines," workovers and the preparation of one previously producing well at the company's Ngo field off the coast of Nigeria for gas injection.
The company, serving notice its cash resources were limited, also said it would postpone a planned debt financing and was "reviewing different alternatives to meet its short-term cash requirements."
The firm said at the end of May it planned to offer US$160 million in senior notes and had filed a preliminary prospectus for the debt issue.
Company officials were not immediately available for comment.
Abacan stock in Toronto hit an all-time high of 15.50 on January 20.
